evidence: Cic. Sest. 32: nūlla Rōmae societās vectīgālium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a partnership for trade, and the companies that farmed the public revenues; Morgan–Owens gives it for a modern company, and societās mercātōria for a trading one.
Traupman’s word for “a business”; classically business, work, an affair (see business).

phrases.latin: numquam est fidēlis cum potente societās
phrases.english: a partnership with the powerful is never to be trusted

phrases.latin: Parva est societās nostra; decem tantum sumus.
phrases.english: Ours is a small company; there are only ten of us.

sources: Lewis & Short: societas · Lewis & Short: negotium
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. corporation, company.
